verdict.reason:
The reviewer's factual claim checks out: comment-ops.ts, comments.controller.ts, slide-ops.ts, slides.controller.ts, tabs.controller.ts (delete/move/duplicate), worksheet-images.ts, board-tree.ts (wired into docs-content.controller.ts), and the CLI comments/sheets-images commands all exist and are fully implemented (verified by reading each file). The paired docs/tasks/active/20260904-class-b-backend-endpoints-lessons.md also narrates lessons from having built exactly this work, confirming it was done. So the todo file's unchecked boxes for steps 2–7 are indeed stale relative to the shipped code.

However, under this lens's rubric this is not a blocking category. It is not steering/injection text, not a secret, not a dangerous instruction, and it is not the 'documentation contradicted by code' pattern as defined (a flag/command/endpoint the prose *promises* that the diff does not provide) — here the code provides *more* than the checklist admits, i.e. stale project-tracking bookkeeping inside a todo file, not a broken promise to a user of the software. The rubric explicitly places task-file conventions (docs/tasks/active/*-todo.md paired with *-lessons.md, checklist state) in the 'craft, not a gate' bucket: 'Repo conventions are also yours, but as craft, not as a gate: task files are docs/tasks/active/YYYYMMDD-<slug>-todo.md paired with -lessons.md...'. An unchecked box on already-shipped work is exactly that kind of craft/staleness issue, capped at nit, not a major blocking defect in this lens.
